title: Operational Amplifiers
intro: An op amp is a high-gain differential amplifier meant to be used inside a feedback loop. Modern op amp design is not a hunt for the ideal amplifier but a compromise: choose the topology that meets the gain, speed, swing, noise and power that this particular application needs (Razavi, Chapter 9).

items: Telescopic cascode: one current path with cascodes stacked on the input pair. Highest speed, lowest power and noise, medium gain, but little swing and an awkward input/output common-mode relationship.

Folded cascode: the input pair's current is folded into cascodes of the opposite type. Input and output common-mode levels can be equal and the input range is wider, at the cost of more power, more noise, lower gain and a lower non-dominant pole.
Two-stage: a high-gain first stage followed by a common-source output stage. Highest gain and rail-to-rail-minus-two-overdrive output swing, but slower and in need of frequency compensation.
Gain-boosted (regulated) cascode: an auxiliary amplifier raises the output resistance of a one-stage op amp to two-stage levels while keeping most of its speed, at the price of power and complexity.
Gain: telescopic medium, folded cascode medium, two-stage high, gain-boosted high.
Output swing: telescopic medium, folded cascode medium, two-stage highest, gain-boosted medium.
Speed: telescopic highest, folded cascode high, two-stage low, gain-boosted medium.
Power: telescopic low, folded cascode medium, two-stage medium, gain-boosted high.
Noise: telescopic low, folded cascode medium, two-stage low, gain-boosted medium.

blocks.text: This ranking is Razavi's Table 9.1. In low-voltage designs the output swing usually decides: with supplies near 1 V, stacking five transistors leaves almost no room, which is why two-stage op amps dominate nanometer designs.

Fully differential op amps double the swing and reject supply and substrate noise, but any high-gain differential stage needs common-mode feedback to pin its output common-mode level. Large steps make every op amp slew. Supply noise and device noise set the floor on accuracy.

items: Op Amp Performance and One-Stage Op Amps: specifications, simple and telescopic op amps, design procedure and linear scaling.

blocks.title: Picking a topology
blocks.text: A switched-capacitor stage at 0.9 V supply needs 0.8 V of single-ended output swing and a DC gain above 60 dB. Which topology is the natural start?
solution: A telescopic or folded cascode stacks four to five devices: with about 0.15 V per overdrive, the swing left at 0.9 V is a few hundred millivolts at most.
A two-stage op amp gives the swing (each output can come within one overdrive of each rail) and two gain stages reach 60 dB; it needs Miller compensation and two-stage CMFB.
